data.long_meaning: Grahansh is a name derived from Sanskrit, which means 'Grabber of Gods'. It is a powerful name that evokes a sense of strength and devotion to the divine. In Hindu mythology, Grahansh is believed to be a name of various deities, particularly those who possess the power to control the planets and celestial bodies. The name Grahansh carries the meaning “Grabber of Gods” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Grahansh usually hope their child will grow to embody grabber of gods and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: The sage Grahansh was a celebrated ascetic and a great devotee of Lord Shiva. He is mentioned in the ancient Indian epics, the Mahabharata and the Ramayana.
historical_references.context: Grahansh is revered for his deep devotion and austerities, and is believed to have attained divine blessings from Lord Shiva. The epics contain several stories about his life and his encounters with various gods and goddesses.

historical_references.reference: Grahansh is also mentioned in the Puranic texts, specifically the Shiva Purana and the Linga Purana. He is described as a great yogi and a powerful sorcerer, who performed severe penances to please Lord Shiva.
historical_references.context: According to the Puranic texts, Grahansh's devotion to Lord Shiva was so intense that he was granted the boon of being able to assume any form he desired. He is also believed to have played a significant role in the divine play of Lord Shiva and his consort Parvati.
